summary: This sermon distinguishes between healthy, protective fear and debilitating anxiety, arguing that anxiety arises when we place our identity in temporary things rather than in God. Using 2 Timothy 1:7 and David's flight from Absalom in Psalm 3, the speaker teaches four steps to overcome anxiety: follow your thread back to God, relocate your glory from finite things to God alone, remember Christ as your substitute for sin, and remember your purpose in serving others.
key_points: Healthy fear is God's gift for immediate danger; anxiety is paralyzing and comes from placing identity in finite things
Christians face three enemies—the devil, the flesh, and the world—that seek to destroy peace and joy
David's example in Psalm 3 shows refocusing from fear to God's protection despite real danger and threatened identity
Four steps to overcome anxiety: follow your thread back to God, relocate your glory in eternal things, see Christ as your substitute, remember your mission to others
big_idea: God calls us to exchange debilitating anxiety for power, love, and a sound mind by anchoring our identity in Him rather than in temporary, finite things.
title: Healthy Fear?
